newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Scaw to buy Malbak Haggie stake.
newsitem.headline: Scaw to buy Malbak Haggie stake.

text.p: Scaw Metals, a division of Amic Industries Ltd, has agreed to buy a further 16 percent stake in Haggie Ltd from Malbak Ltd at a purchase price of 25 rand a share, the firms said in a joint statement Monday.
At the same time Business Day newspaper reported that Malbak had sold its unlisted subsidiary Malbak Motor Holdings (MMH) to Sankorp for 265 million rand.

The paper said the agreement with Sankorp, which is the majority shareholder in Malbak, had been reached late last week and would be effective from March 1. Sankorp would pay cash for the purchase, the paper said.
In terms of the Haggie agreement, the statement said that Amic Industries had agreed in principle to buy 3.4 million shares in Haggie from Malbak, paying in cash for the purchase.

As Amic Industries already holds a 36 percent stake in Haggie, having joint control of the company with Malbak which also owns 36 percent, Amic Industries' holding will increase to approximately 52 percent.

Malbak will distribute its remaining 20 percent holding in Haggie pro-rata to its own shareholders on the basis of 1.24 Haggie shares for every 100 Malbak shares held. This would be done simultaneously with the distribution of Malbak's other listed holdings.

The sales form part of Malbak's decision to unbundle its assets to its shareholders. A Malbak spokesman told Business Day that the unbundling process would be complete once negotiations for the sale of its controlling stake in computer company ICL had been concluded.
